overview: The Kom'rk-class Fighter is a assault fighter whose service history spans Clone Wars through Imperial Era. Mandalorian Gauntlet fighters used by Death Watch and Clan Kryze, capable of atmospheric and space combat. Imperial archives, Rebel intelligence briefings, and Mandalorian shipyard records estimate total production at ~800 units, though wartime losses and black-market refits make exact counts difficult to verify.
history:
Design bureaus first drafted the Kom'rk-class Fighter during the political tensions that defined Clone Wars through Imperial Era. Engineers prioritised capabilities suited to its role as a assault fighter, balancing armour, manoeuvrability, and crew requirements against the industrial capacity of the factions that ordered it into production.

As fleet doctrine evolved, the Kom'rk-class Fighter entered front-line service in convoy escort, planetary assault, and deep-space patrol missions. Mandalorian Gauntlet fighters used by Death Watch and Clan Kryze, capable of atmospheric and space combat. Veterans praised its reliability under fire while analysts debated whether mass production at ~800 units diluted quality control across shipyard lines.

Major campaigns cemented the vessel's reputation — whether as a terror weapon, a rebel lifeline, or a smuggler's last hope. Battle damage reports show the assault fighter could absorb punishment that would destroy lighter craft, though attrition rates climbed sharply during the bloodiest years of galactic war.

In the modern era, surviving hulls appear in private collections, museum orbits, and covert fleets. Restorers hunt spare parts across scrap worlds while historians argue the Kom'rk-class Fighter symbolises the industrial scale of conflict more than any single battle honour.
significance:
The Kom'rk-class Fighter illustrates how shipwright traditions and wartime desperation combine to shape galactic warfare. Its assault fighter layout influenced successor designs long after production lines fell silent.

Approximately ~800 units hulls served during Clone Wars through Imperial Era, making the class one of the most visible symbols of its faction's naval power. Colour markings and unit insignia turned anonymous factory output into icons recognised across holonet broadcasts.

For engineers and tacticians, the Kom'rk-class Fighter remains a case study in trade-offs between firepower, crew survival, and maintenance — lessons still taught at academies from Coruscant to Mandalore.
